rejected.title: How technology changes reading
card: A digital text is a text read on a screen, such as a news site, a blog or a social media post. It can use features that a printed page cannot.
Links
words or images that take the reader to another page. Readers can jump between texts instead of reading in one set order.
Video and comments
a digital text can include video and sound, and readers can reply in a comment box. This lets readers respond to a text and add to it.
Scrolling on a screen also changes reading. Readers often skim, so writers use short paragraphs and headings to catch attention.
rejected.remember: Digital texts let readers choose their path, watch and listen, and reply.

a.q: Ava reads a news article online. She taps a link in the second paragraph and ends up on a different page. What feature of digital texts is this?
opts: Readers can choose their own path between texts
Readers can reply to the writer in a comment box
Readers can watch and hear the story as a video
Readers often skim short paragraphs and headings
a.why: A link takes the reader to another page, so the reader chooses where to go next instead of reading in one set order. A comment box is for replying, which Ava did not do.
a.clue: Think about what a link lets a reader do.

b.q: Sam posts a short video review of a book on a school website. Classmates write replies under it. How has technology changed how people respond to this text?
opts: Readers can reply under it and add to the text
Readers can jump to another page through a link
Readers can skim by looking at the headings
Readers read in one set order, as on a printed page
b.why: The classmates replied under the video, so their comments respond to the review and become part of the page. Links do change how people read, but no one used a link here.
b.clue: Look at what the classmates did under the video.

flags: Question b, wording: The stem says classmates 'write replies under it', and the right option repeats this as 'reply under it'. A student could match the words without knowing the idea.
